hypothesis: A causal pivot CE target with maker-first BUY and risk-reducing-IOC SELL can improve quote uptime and inventory drawdown without collapsing executable BUY fills or round trips.
expectedResult: Across non-overlapping score windows, candidate execution remains sufficiently diverse and executable, quote uptime improves without excessive refresh churn, max drawdown does not worsen, and route decisions match the declared maker/IOC contract.
actualResult: The declared maker-first/risk-reducing-IOC candidate does not maintain executable BUY participation across the two checked windows. In the current window it increases uptime but produces zero BUY fills and zero round trips; in the prior non-overlapping window it collapses to one SELL fill and 2.976% uptime. Changing only BUY route to IOC recovers BUY/round-trip diversity in the current window but does not recover it in the prior window.
rootCause: The causal target can move to a hard low-inventory target while terminal-wealth rejection leaves a non-bilateral base plan; the continuity floor is intentionally not applied in that state, so the candidate can stop quoting despite an exposure-increasing target gap.
The maker-first BUY route explicitly suppresses every Fast BUY IOC request, even when the passive maker path produces no executable BUY fill in the replay window.
Several candidate BUY target gaps are below exchange minimum quantity, so changing route alone cannot make those requests executable without an independent, pre-declared target/quantity rule.
Private maker calibration is insufficient and queueMultiplier=0 remains an assumption; live/replay execution parity is not established.
competingExplanations: The replay maker-fill and callback model may underrepresent live passive BUY fills; this remains unresolved until private maker calibration and parity are completed.
The observed target boundary may be regime-specific, but the same failure pattern appears in both checked windows and must not be dismissed as a single-window artifact.
The current causal target prior/actuation parameters may be too extreme, but changing them is a separate pre-registered experiment and is not justified by these results alone.
missedGates: Quote uptime versus refresh-churn and quote-life gate
requiredPrevention: Do not promote either maker-first or buy-IOC control based on these replay results.
Require a pre-declared multi-window criterion for BUY participation, round trips, fill ratio, uptime, churn, and drawdown before route selection.
Keep minimum quantity/notional, stale-BBO, adverse-selection, inventory hard-limit, terminal-wealth, and SELL risk-reducing safety gates unchanged.
Add an explicit observable distinction between target-restoring exposure-increasing BUY rejection, risk-reducing SELL actuation, and maker-first route suppression.
Collect the missing independent private maker samples, including BUY-side samples, and calibrate a non-zero queue model before economic tuning.
Add persisted-episode route integration replay for callback ordering, latency, partial fills, reservation timing, stale-BBO replan, and maker-first quote planning.

Run at least one additional non-overlapping window with the same frozen parameters.
Re-run focused and race tests after any source change.
Re-run calibrated/private-fill and live/replay parity gates.
